patch_description: The current algorithm sends each partition of the data from src to every destination independently via Dijkstra, so shared link segments are traversed once per (dst, partition) — causing massive redundant transfers and high cost. Key improvement: treat the broadcast as a Steiner-tree-like shared delivery problem. For each partition, find a set of paths to all destinations that maximally share edges, so each shared edge is only paid for once across the destinations it serves. Concretely: (1) add a small epsilon to all edge costs so Dijkstra prefers fewer hops (fewer, longer-shared links), (2) greedily route destinations one at a time over the cheapest available path in a residual graph where edges already used for this partition are free (cost ~0) — this reuses shared trunk links and only pays for the diverging tails, (3) drop unreachable destinations gracefully instead of crashing. This dramatically reduces total data transfer cost while keeping the API (BroadCastTopology, append_dst_partition_path) unchanged.
